thread:
maya: Quick check — reordering the left rail groups (Workloads, Models, Observability) into a compact hierarchy feels cleaner on paper. Thoughts on how this interacts with deep-links? I noticed some routes break when we collapse groups.

tj: I'm worried about the route contract. We currently use /apps/:appId/:section/:sub where :section maps to group id. If we rename groups, bookmarks/links break.

devon: We can add redirects in the router layer — keep a stable slug->id map for v1. That preserves links but adds lookup complexity.

eli: Accessibility: when groups collapse, focus order shifts. We need a programmatic focus reset when a group expands/collapses — aria-expanded + move focus to the first child.

maya: Good call. Do we have a simple pattern? aria-controls + send focus to first item when expanded?

tj: Yes. Also for keyboard users, keep a roving tabindex on top-level items. That prevents losing keyboard focus when DOM order changes.

maya: Small UI nit — focus ring is barely visible on dark mode for the compact rail. Anyone else see it?

eli: I filed a quick reproducer: our outline token uses alpha 0 on dark. Fix is to use a dedicated dark-mode focus token or invert the color in dark.

devon: For deep links, I'd prefer decoupling display name from slug. Slug -> canonical id mapping in router allows renaming without breaking URLs.

maya: Agree. Can we add a migration table? Example: { 'models-v1': 'models', 'deploys-v1': 'deployments' } as a transient map.

tj: That works. We should also expose a deprecation banner in the console when an old slug is used (to notify internal teams).

eli: Breadcrumb accessibility: breadcrumb currently duplicates visible label; add aria-current to the active crumb and ensure separators are aria-hidden. Screen readers will be much clearer.

maya: Action items: 1) devon — add slug map + redirects, 2) tj — implement roving tabindex and focus reset, 3) eli — propose focus token fix for dark mode and add aria-current to breadcrumbs. I will follow up with copy tweaks for compact labels.

maya: Quick follow-up — do we ship this as a minor nav tweak or treat as a migration? It depends on redirect strategy and telemetry.

devon: If we implement redirects automatically and keep canonical ids, safe to ship as minor. But we need rollout + telemetry to catch edge cases (old bookmarks, third-party links).

tj: Can we gate the change behind a feature flag (console.nav.reorder) and run a 10% canary?

maya: Yes. 10% canary sounds good. I'll open a PR with the design tokens, screenshots, and a short migration guide.

eli: I'll add accessibility test cases to the PR — keyboard nav, ARIA attributes, and screen-reader announcements.

maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:

tj: lgtm

devon: on it

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: console.nav.reorder -> 10% at 2026-04-01T18:00Z
